clue.text: Best replacement, a bit less than stellar?

indicators.note: a bit less than the full word means its final letter is dropped here

parts.note: stellar means starry, full of stars

explanation.surface: A substitute player is judged not quite stellar compared with the star he replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like 'finest', but it is Pete Best, the Beatles drummer whom Ringo Starr replaced in 1962.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo took over the drum stool from Pete Best, so he was literally the replacement for Best.

clue.text: Ordeals of following lines in petition on phones

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first part above the second
in places the abbreviation inside the petition word

parts.note: to sue is to petition or appeal
ff. is the abbreviation for following lines or pages
rings means phones, telephones someone

explanation.surface: The trials of the next lines in a plea made over the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordeals are painful trials, and sufferings are the hardships endured in them.

clue.text: Overbearing Arthur cuddles frequent companion for (dishy) Josh

indicators.note: cuddles means holds close, so the short name wraps around the companion word

parts.note: Art is a short form of the name Arthur
rogan josh is a curry dish, so rogan is Josh's usual partner on a menu

explanation.surface: A domineering Arthur hugs the regular partner of handsome Josh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishy' suggests attractive; in brackets it tells you this Josh is a dish: rogan josh, the Indian lamb curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Overbearing and arrogant are synonyms for haughty, domineering behaviour.

clue.text: Bridesmaid turning more chaste when worried nun enters

indicators.note: enters means the jumbled letters go inside the reversed word
turning means the more-chaste word is read backwards

parts.note: purer means more chaste, more innocent

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters of nun are mixed up

explanation.surface: A wedding attendant grows more virtuous when an anxious nun turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'always the bridesmaid, never the bride': someone who keeps finishing second.
explanation.definitionFit: A perpetual bridesmaid is figuratively one who comes second, the person finishing just behind the winner.

clue.text: Weight of ring in purple and very very black

parts.note: plum is a shade of purple

indicators.note: in places the ring shape inside the string of black grades

parts.note: BBB is a pencil grading for very soft, very black lead; each extra B is another very
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A description of a heavy object coloured purple and intensely black, set with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Pencil leads are graded B, BB, BBB for increasing blackness, so 'very very black' is BBB.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb bob is the lead weight hung on a line to find the true vertical.

clue.text: Col. Blimp, at bottom a buffoon

indicators.note: at bottom in a down clue means the last letter of Blimp

parts.note: an ass is a fool, a buffoon

explanation.surface: Colonel Blimp is, at heart, a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Col. Blimp' reads as the pompous cartoon colonel; 'Col.' is really a col, a gap in a mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a low point between two peaks, the route through a mountain range.

clue.text: Essence of male orientation symbol

parts.note: an arrow is a sign showing direction

explanation.surface: The heart of the matter in the sign for men, the circle with an arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The marrow of something is its innermost core, its essence or vital part.

clue.text: Large mammal's horny plates enable scuffling

indicators.note: scuffling means jostling about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A big animal's hard plates allow it to brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen is the comb-like keratin plating in the mouths of filter-feeding whales.

clue.text: Promotion neglecting small computer start-up

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving out, so the small letter is removed

parts.note: a boost is a push or promotion

explanation.surface: Marketing that ignores a little tech firm just starting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start-up' suggests a new firm; here it is starting a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Booting a computer means starting it up, loading its operating system.

clue.text: Strength of monkeys regularly seen in trees

indicators.note: seen in places the picked letters inside the trees

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of monkeys is taken

explanation.surface: A remark on the power of monkeys often spotted up in the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness is solidity or resolve, a kind of strength of body or will.

clue.text: Mount races to capture heart of Maureen O'Hara in a film

indicators.note: to capture means the climbing word and races hold a letter inside

parts.note: to mount a wall is to scale it

indicators.note: heart of means the central letter of Maureen is taken

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorbike races

explanation.surface: Climbing and racing to win over the actress Maureen O'Hara for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Maureen O'Hara the actress is a red herring: the film O'Hara is the heroine of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine of the film Gone with the Wind, played by Vivien Leigh.

clue.text: Mostly faddish argument over loose clothing

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: cult, as in a cult film, means fashionable among a following

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or argument

explanation.surface: Fashion-conscious types fall out over baggy garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Culottes are wide, loose-fitting women's shorts cut to look like a skirt.

clue.text: One's learned what breaks short knife, in hindsight

indicators.note: in hindsight means looking back, so the built word is read backwards
breaks means the query word splits the knife open
short means the knife loses its last letter

parts.note: a dagger is a short stabbing knife
eh is the spoken query meaning what?

explanation.surface: Someone has discovered what snaps a cut-down blade, but only after the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what' stands for the query 'eh?'. 'short' leaves DAGGE; 'breaks' gives DAEHGGE, which 'in hindsight' turns round. 'One's learned' is read as 'one who is learned'.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual or scholarly person is informally called this, so it fits a learned one.

clue.text: Shimmering steel blue turns around, never going out of style

indicators.note: around means the reversed word goes outside the jumbled letters
turns means the blue word is read backwards

parts.note: blue means sad, low in spirits

indicators.note: shimmering suggests wavering movement, so the letters of steel are mixed

explanation.surface: Gleaming blue steel always looks fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless has no date attached; it is classic and never goes out of fashion.

clue.text: Leeway of little magnitude in a cavalry weapon

indicators.note: in places the small-size word inside the cavalry weapon phrase

parts.note: a lance is the long spear carried by cavalry
low means of little size or degree

explanation.surface: How much latitude a small spear-carrying cavalryman is given.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a margin of tolerance, the same idea as leeway or latitude given.

clue.text: Someone helping seabird in the past, according to appearances?

parts.note: ex means former, from the past
a tern is a seabird
an ally is a supporter, someone helping

explanation.surface: An old helper of a seabird, judging by how things look.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwardly, judged by the outside surface, is how things appear; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Treat to spy? Thing quite different!

definitions.text: Treat to spy? Thing quite different!

indicators.note: quite different means the letters of these words are rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something pleasing to look at; or rather, the very opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: the opposite of a feast for the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly is the opposite of a treat for the eyes, so it is quite different from one.

clue.text: Mum crossing Thames at Oxford hugs somebody vacant like mummy's boy?

indicators.note: crossing means the mum word spans the river, set on either side

parts.note: sh! means keep mum, be quiet

indicators.note: hugs means the river name goes round the emptied word

parts.note: the Thames at Oxford is called the Isis

indicators.note: vacant means the inside is emptied, leaving the outer letters of somebody

explanation.surface: Silence spans the Oxford river, with someone empty-headed and soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, matching 'mummy's boy'; it means keep quiet, SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mummy's boy is thought effeminate or timid, and sissyish means wimpish in that way.

clue.text: More hip from good jumper to compete at start of run-up

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a jumper
to vie is to compete

indicators.note: at start of means the first letter of run-up is taken

explanation.surface: A cooler athlete: a good jumper competing at the start of the run-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater or an athlete; it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Groovy is dated slang for fashionable, so groovier means more hip.

clue.text: Get French cheeses picked up for a drink with vodka

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: get means see (understand), and Bries are soft French cheeses

explanation.surface: Fetch some French cheese to go with a vodka cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sea Breeze is a cocktail of vodka with cranberry and grapefruit juice.

clue.text: It's entirely about protecting university

indicators.note: protecting means the outer words shield the letter inside

parts.note: all means wholly, entirely
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Everything concerns protecting the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun; it is the noun meaning sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is old slang for sex appeal, an attractive magnetism, the same as charm.

clue.text: Pushed a blockage through, not even having flushed 14

indicators.note: 14 points to the answer of 14 Down, meaning on the outside, so the flushed word sits outside

parts.note: flushed means red in the face
odd means not even

explanation.surface: Clearing a drain with a rod, though the flushing went unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flushed' suggests a toilet; it means red-faced. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rod a drain is to clear it by pushing rods through the blockage.

clue.text: He devised cuts since accordingly introduced by young man

indicators.note: introduced by means put inside the young man word

parts.note: a son is a young man of the family
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
so means therefore, accordingly

explanation.surface: A man who designed spending reductions, brought in by a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' suggests budget cuts; here they are haircuts. Vidal Sassoon was the celebrated hairdresser behind the bob cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidal Sassoon, the famous hair stylist, created influential haircuts such as the five-point bob.

clue.text: Logic's abandoned with theologian involved in popularity-based award

indicators.note: involved in means the theologian goes inside the jumbled letters
abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Reason is thrown out when a divine gets involved in a popular award.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold disc is awarded to a record for reaching a sales threshold, so it measures popularity.

clue.text: Someone obsessing about computer language without introduction of recursion

indicators.note: without means the letter is removed from the language

parts.note: Greek is a language

indicators.note: introduction of means the first letter of recursion is taken

explanation.surface: A computer fanatic speaking a programming language without recursion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computer language' reads as a programming language; the definition stops at 'computer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd fixated on technology, especially computers, is informally called this.

clue.text: Nothing in arrest leads to place of confinement

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the arrest word

parts.note: to cop is slang for to arrest, nab
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing in an arrest leads to a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is a pen for poultry, and figuratively any cramped enclosure where one is shut in.

clue.text: Revocation of secular condition Foreign Office authorised

indicators.note: revocation means calling back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: laic means lay, non-clerical, secular
if introduces a condition
FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the UK foreign ministry

explanation.surface: Britain's foreign ministry has sanctioned overturning a requirement to be secular.
explanation.definitionFit: Something official carries the sanction of authority, so it is authorised.

clue.text: Thoroughly involved with demand in store

indicators.note: in places the demand word inside the store word

parts.note: to keep something is to store it
a need is a demand or requirement

explanation.surface: Fully engaged, with requests piling up in the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deeply immersed in a matter is idiomatically being up to your knees in it.

clue.text: Run right into perhaps a baleful badger

indicators.note: into means the two letters go inside the fodder word

parts.note: a bale is full of hay, so hay is an example of a baleful
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A menacing badger hurrying along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baleful' looks like 'menacing' but is read as 'bale-full': what fills a bale, i.e. hay.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger and to harry are synonyms: both mean to pester or harass persistently.
